Execution evidence · CycloneDX 1.6

A signed run,
in a standard parts list.

An ingredients label, with a signed receipt stapled in. See the files that ran, the room they ran in, and what came back. Further down, a referee's verdict goes into the same label.

A bill of materials (BOM) is a parts list for software. CycloneDX is the Open Worldwide Application Security Project’s standard format for that list. This example puts one run into the list. The image’s own ingredients label is linked separately when supplied.

Plimsoll runs code in a sandbox, like a locked room. A digest is a fingerprint of some bytes, made here with the SHA-256 hash algorithm. Change one letter and the fingerprint changes. The request is the files and commands sent into the room. The result is what came back.

The daemon, a long-running server named plimsolld, returns a run record: the fingerprints, image, room’s isolation tier and times. A harness, a separate checking program, checks that record and seals it. We call that sealed record the receipt. The seal is a tamper strip, like the one on a medicine bottle.

The signed wrapper is a Dead Simple Signing Envelope (DSSE). Inside it, an in-toto statement is a standard way to write a claim. CycloneDX Attestations (CDXA) attach the receipt as evidence for the list’s three claims: code, image and isolation.

This converter needs a selected OCI manifest identity, the exact fingerprint of one container image for one platform. Today that means docker on the containerd image store. Other providers’ runs are refused when that identity is missing.

The record is signed. The BOM is unsigned. The seal lets you spot changed evidence. It does not independently measure the room’s walls. The daemon supplies those facts. A key included with the receipt shows which key checks the seal; you still need an independently trusted key to know the signer.

The evidence path

From execution to a checkable file

1. RequestThe program's files, commands, minimum isolation tier and timeout.
2. RecordThe daemon's statement of what was sent, returned and used to run it.
3. BundleThe harness checks fingerprints, then signs records and entry links.
4. BOMThe emitter checks the bundle. A reviewer can rebuild the mapping from it.
How thick were the walls

Four rooms, two were used

plimsoll runs code in a locked room and says which room. The tier names below are the technical words; the pictures are what they mean.

Click a room. The reconcile runs asked for at least kernel, and the same request was then sent to a VM, which is thicker, so it ran there too; the adapter runs in the verdict section asked for at least container. A daemon offering a thinner wall than the floor refuses to run it, and nothing is dispatched.

The tier is what the configuration says plus the checks the daemon runs at startup, never a hardware measurement. The run's record names it, and the seal covers the name.

What a receipt holds

A till receipt for one run

Read it like a receipt

CODE and RESULT are fingerprints: a short code computed from the bytes, which changes completely if one letter changes. IMAGE is the fingerprint of the frozen filesystem the code ran in. WALL is the room. GRANT says whether the code was allowed to reach anything outside, and here it was not. TIME is the daemon's own clock.

The seal is a tamper strip, like the one on a medicine bottle: a signature over the whole receipt. Peel it, change one character, and it no longer fits. The box below this run lets you do exactly that in your browser.

The values printed on the drawing are the first run's, shortened; the full ones are in each run's section.

One network attempt, two settings

The failure is preserved with its evidence

The program attempts to fetch https://example.com/. Its own five-second timer bounds the demonstration, so it cannot wait indefinitely. The sandboxed attempt failed; the outside transcript reports success.

Inside plimsoll

Signed exchange

node egress.js
Exit 3, duration 5373 milliseconds.

egress: refused: TimeoutError

The word “refused” comes from the guest program. Its fetch timer expired; the sandbox timeout flag is false. The timeout is consistent with the provider's reported network configuration, but does not independently establish its cause.

Outside plimsoll

Unsigned transcript
# record: 29c2e7b07429f25bbedda4f4572b4720837437bbf1f6e924a75d7d44739509d6
# step: node egress.js
# The same egress attempt outside plimsoll
#
# Command, run on the developer machine on 2026-10-13 with the node on PATH (v26.3.1),
# default network, no sandbox, no record of any kind:
#
#   node egress.js
#
# Output and exit code, pasted by hand (there is no signed record to cite):

egress: reached example.com, status 200
exit code: 0

The same file reached the internet outside the room, while nobody wrote a signed receipt. This text was pasted by hand. There is nothing sealed for the converter to staple into a BOM. The two settings also used different runtimes; this comparison does not establish why the inside attempt failed.

And a third time, the same file in a Docker Cloud microVM, a separate building whose account network policy denies every connection: exit 3 after 5548 milliseconds, sandbox timeout flag false, under its own signed receipt.

egress: refused: TimeoutError

One failed request is an observed result, not a universal proof that every network path is blocked. The full sandbox boundary still rests on the daemon and its provider checks.

What sits where

An ingredients label with the receipt stapled in

Why a label

Software already ships with an ingredients label, the SBOM (software bill of materials): a list of every package inside. An AI agent's program is a new kind of ingredient with no package name, no version and no maintainer, so it never made the label. This file is that label for one run, with the receipt stapled in as evidence behind three claims.

The rows are what any viewer shows: the program and its file fingerprints, the image, the run. The staple is the part most viewers do not draw yet: the sealed receipt inside the declarations block. A platform that gives you back the original file lets you check it; this page checks it for you below.

The verdict

Did the robot go where it was told?

The receipt says what ran and where. It does not say whether the code did its job. For that somebody has to check the work, and the check has to come from the other side of the counter.

The setup, in plain words. A fleet vendor sells robots you drive through a web API (the robots are simulated; no warehouse was harmed). An AI wrote an adapter: the small program that turns the platform's orders ("robot two, go to aisle ten") into that vendor's API calls. Before the platform lets it near a real fleet it wants one answer: does the adapter do what it says it does?

So the platform runs the adapter inside plimsoll with a grant that reaches the vendor's API and nothing else, hands it a plan of four commands, and then asks the vendor what happened: which orders arrived, for which robots, and where each robot stopped. A referee compares that account with the plan under eight rules. The adapter's own report is checked against the vendor's ledger; it never gets to grade itself. The referee signs the result as a qualification statement bound to the run's receipt, and this page staples that statement into the same ingredients label as a fourth claim with a conformance score: 1 when every rule held, 0 when any broke. Conformance is CycloneDX's word for "how well the thing meets a requirement"; here the requirement is "met the platform's rules".

✓An adapter that passed all 8 rulesadapter-v2.js in scenario nominal: all 8 rules held. Conformance 1. Click for the rules and the receipt.✗An adapter that broke one ruleadapter-v1.js in scenario lost_ack: 1 of 8 rules broken. Conformance 0. Click for the rules and the receipt.

About the one that failed. In the scenario called lost_ack the vendor accepts robot r2's order, starts it, and then the answer gets lost on the way back (a 503, "service unavailable"). The first adapter did the natural thing and sent the order again. The robot, being a robot, did as it was told, twice. Rule four, one order per command, caught it from the ledger: run04-c2 became 2 orders (m2, m3). The rewritten adapter sends a command identifier the vendor recognizes, so a repeat is answered with the original order and the robot gets one trip. Nothing in the adapter's own report would have told you this. The ledger did, which is why the referee reads the ledger.

What this is not: an independent audit (the platform wrote the rules and signed the verdict), a real vendor (the ledger comes from the simulator the adapter example ships), or proof of who wrote the adapter. What it is: a verdict someone else can re-derive from the same evidence, which is what a score in a label ought to mean. The Go checker re-runs the eight rules from the attached statement; your browser checks the seal, the binding to this receipt, and that the claim says what the statement says. The runs, the rules and all 38 verdicts are on INTERNAL · the adapter example page →.

The signed source exchange

The run

Outcome: completedStated tier: kernelFloor asked: kernelNo grant: no networkBundle line 1

The completed outcome means the runner returned a normal result; a step with a nonzero exit code still failed. The stated tier is the daemon's reported isolation tier, backed by provider configuration and startup checks, never runtime attestation.

The program's files

reconcile.js

SHA-256: c2de8205ca1e811fba188b71b051e25644f88b8190351372ab3ed4a842231456

// reconcile.js: match payments to invoices by invoice id and report what is
// unpaid, overpaid or matched. Amounts are integer cents.
function reconcile(invoices, payments) {
  const paid = new Map();
  for (const p of payments) paid.set(p.invoice, (paid.get(p.invoice) || 0) + p.cents);
  const matched = [], unpaid = [], overpaid = [];
  for (const inv of invoices) {
    const got = paid.get(inv.id) || 0;
    if (got === inv.cents) matched.push(inv.id);
    else if (got < inv.cents) unpaid.push({ id: inv.id, owed: inv.cents - got });
    else overpaid.push({ id: inv.id, excess: got - inv.cents });
  }
  return { matched, unpaid, overpaid };
}
module.exports = { reconcile };
reconcile.test.js

SHA-256: ce76efdec6de19969e12f5ca27b273396ca274dfa330df36811f78354c659c97

const assert = require("node:assert/strict");
const { reconcile } = require("./reconcile.js");
const invoices = [
  { id: "INV-1001", cents: 12500 },
  { id: "INV-1002", cents: 8000 },
  { id: "INV-1003", cents: 4200 },
];
const payments = [
  { invoice: "INV-1001", cents: 12500 },
  { invoice: "INV-1002", cents: 5000 },
  { invoice: "INV-1003", cents: 4200 },
  { invoice: "INV-1003", cents: 300 },
];
const r = reconcile(invoices, payments);
assert.deepEqual(r.matched, ["INV-1001"]);
assert.deepEqual(r.unpaid, [{ id: "INV-1002", owed: 3000 }]);
assert.deepEqual(r.overpaid, [{ id: "INV-1003", excess: 300 }]);
console.log("reconcile: 3 assertions passed");

The commands and recorded results

Standard output (stdout) is printed output; standard error (stderr) is the separate diagnostic channel. Exit code 0 means the command reported success. A nonzero code means it reported failure.

Try the receipt here

The seal is a tamper strip, like the one on a medicine bottle. Check it, then change a copy and watch the seal fail. Your browser uses only the bytes inside this page.

Checking whether this browser can verify the seal.

    This checks one receipt, its bundle line's seal and its JSON fields. The emitter's Go checker also verifies the whole bundle when it has it and proves that the JSON copy matches the stored protobuf messages. An attached public key proves consistency under that key; it does not tell you who owns it.

    Checks actually run by the emitter

    These receipts come from checking the generated BOM and three separately altered copies. The original source files are unchanged.

    PASS: CycloneDX 1.6 schema (vendored, offline).
PASS: DSSE envelope signature and run-record digest.
PASS: the attached bundle line: its link's seal and place, the stored request and result against the signed digests.
PASS: exchange.json equals the line's protobuf messages and reproduces their digests.
PASS: file-set digest recomputed from file components and bound to the signed request.
PASS: every mapped field and claim matches the verified exchange.
PASS: attached key matches independently trusted key.
PASS: the attached line is line 1 of the referenced bundle, whole to its checkpoint (8 lines).
LIMIT: names, page URL and assessor label are unsigned presentation; runtime assertions remain the daemon's statements.
PASS: image SBOM hash, manifest identity and BOM-Link match the local evidence file.
PASS: altered envelope refused: envelope: attest: no valid signature from this key
PASS: altered file hash refused: file-set digest differs from program hash
PASS: altered claim digest refused: BOM differs from the verified exchange: file contents, digests, claims or another mapped field was changed

    reconcile.js

    SHA-256: c2de8205ca1e811fba188b71b051e25644f88b8190351372ab3ed4a842231456

    // reconcile.js: match payments to invoices by invoice id and report what is
// unpaid, overpaid or matched. Amounts are integer cents.
function reconcile(invoices, payments) {
  const paid = new Map();
  for (const p of payments) paid.set(p.invoice, (paid.get(p.invoice) || 0) + p.cents);
  const matched = [], unpaid = [], overpaid = [];
  for (const inv of invoices) {
    const got = paid.get(inv.id) || 0;
    if (got === inv.cents) matched.push(inv.id);
    else if (got < inv.cents) unpaid.push({ id: inv.id, owed: inv.cents - got });
    else overpaid.push({ id: inv.id, excess: got - inv.cents });
  }
  return { matched, unpaid, overpaid };
}
module.exports = { reconcile };
    reconcile.test.js

    SHA-256: ce76efdec6de19969e12f5ca27b273396ca274dfa330df36811f78354c659c97

    const assert = require("node:assert/strict");
const { reconcile } = require("./reconcile.js");
const invoices = [
  { id: "INV-1001", cents: 12500 },
  { id: "INV-1002", cents: 8000 },
  { id: "INV-1003", cents: 4200 },
];
const payments = [
  { invoice: "INV-1001", cents: 12500 },
  { invoice: "INV-1002", cents: 5000 },
  { invoice: "INV-1003", cents: 4200 },
  { invoice: "INV-1003", cents: 300 },
];
const r = reconcile(invoices, payments);
assert.deepEqual(r.matched, ["INV-1001"]);
assert.deepEqual(r.unpaid, [{ id: "INV-1002", owed: 3000 }]);
assert.deepEqual(r.overpaid, [{ id: "INV-1003", excess: 300 }]);
console.log("reconcile: 3 assertions passed");

  { invoice: "INV-2002", cents: 15000 },
  { invoice: "INV-2004", cents: 31000 },
  { invoice: "INV-2004", cents: 1000 },
];

    // egress.js: one benign network attempt, so the record shows what the boundary
// did with it. Outside plimsoll this reaches example.com; inside, with no grant,
// there is no network, and the exit code says so.
fetch("https://example.com/", { signal: AbortSignal.timeout(5000) })
  .then((r) => { console.log("egress: reached example.com, status", r.status); process.exit(0); })
  .catch((e) => { console.error("egress: refused:", (e.cause && e.cause.code) || e.name); process.exit(3); });

      reconcile.js

      SHA-256: c2de8205ca1e811fba188b71b051e25644f88b8190351372ab3ed4a842231456

      // reconcile.js: match payments to invoices by invoice id and report what is
// unpaid, overpaid or matched. Amounts are integer cents.
function reconcile(invoices, payments) {
  const paid = new Map();
  for (const p of payments) paid.set(p.invoice, (paid.get(p.invoice) || 0) + p.cents);
  const matched = [], unpaid = [], overpaid = [];
  for (const inv of invoices) {
    const got = paid.get(inv.id) || 0;
    if (got === inv.cents) matched.push(inv.id);
    else if (got < inv.cents) unpaid.push({ id: inv.id, owed: inv.cents - got });
    else overpaid.push({ id: inv.id, excess: got - inv.cents });
  }
  return { matched, unpaid, overpaid };
}
module.exports = { reconcile };
      reconcile.test.js

      SHA-256: ce76efdec6de19969e12f5ca27b273396ca274dfa330df36811f78354c659c97

      const assert = require("node:assert/strict");
const { reconcile } = require("./reconcile.js");
const invoices = [
  { id: "INV-1001", cents: 12500 },
  { id: "INV-1002", cents: 8000 },
  { id: "INV-1003", cents: 4200 },
];
const payments = [
  { invoice: "INV-1001", cents: 12500 },
  { invoice: "INV-1002", cents: 5000 },
  { invoice: "INV-1003", cents: 4200 },
  { invoice: "INV-1003", cents: 300 },
];
const r = reconcile(invoices, payments);
assert.deepEqual(r.matched, ["INV-1001"]);
assert.deepEqual(r.unpaid, [{ id: "INV-1002", owed: 3000 }]);
assert.deepEqual(r.overpaid, [{ id: "INV-1003", excess: 300 }]);
console.log("reconcile: 3 assertions passed");

An attached public key proves consistency under that key; it does not tell you who owns it.

        reconcile.js

        SHA-256: c2de8205ca1e811fba188b71b051e25644f88b8190351372ab3ed4a842231456

        // reconcile.js: match payments to invoices by invoice id and report what is
// unpaid, overpaid or matched. Amounts are integer cents.
function reconcile(invoices, payments) {
  const paid = new Map();
  for (const p of payments) paid.set(p.invoice, (paid.get(p.invoice) || 0) + p.cents);
  const matched = [], unpaid = [], overpaid = [];
  for (const inv of invoices) {
    const got = paid.get(inv.id) || 0;
    if (got === inv.cents) matched.push(inv.id);
    else if (got < inv.cents) unpaid.push({ id: inv.id, owed: inv.cents - got });
    else overpaid.push({ id: inv.id, excess: got - inv.cents });
  }
  return { matched, unpaid, overpaid };
}
module.exports = { reconcile };
        reconcile.test.js

        SHA-256: ce76efdec6de19969e12f5ca27b273396ca274dfa330df36811f78354c659c97

        const assert = require("node:assert/strict");
const { reconcile } = require("./reconcile.js");
const invoices = [
  { id: "INV-1001", cents: 12500 },
  { id: "INV-1002", cents: 8000 },
  { id: "INV-1003", cents: 4200 },
];
const payments = [
  { invoice: "INV-1001", cents: 12500 },
  { invoice: "INV-1002", cents: 5000 },
  { invoice: "INV-1003", cents: 4200 },
  { invoice: "INV-1003", cents: 300 },
];
const r = reconcile(invoices, payments);
assert.deepEqual(r.matched, ["INV-1001"]);
assert.deepEqual(r.unpaid, [{ id: "INV-1002", owed: 3000 }]);
assert.deepEqual(r.overpaid, [{ id: "INV-1003", excess: 300 }]);
console.log("reconcile: 3 assertions passed");

        // egress.js: one benign network attempt, so the record shows what the boundary
// did with it. Outside plimsoll this reaches example.com; inside, with no grant,
// there is no network, and the exit code says so.
fetch("https://example.com/", { signal: AbortSignal.timeout(5000) })
  .then((r) => { console.log("egress: reached example.com, status", r.status); process.exit(0); })
  .catch((e) => { console.error("egress: refused:", (e.cause && e.cause.code) || e.name); process.exit(3); });

        Checking whether this browser can verify the seal.

          This checks one receipt, its bundle line's seal and its JSON fields. The emitter's Go checker also verifies the whole bundle when it has it and proves that the JSON copy matches the stored protobuf messages. An attached public key proves consistency under that key; it does not tell you who owns it.

          // The platform's conformance harness: loads a vendor adapter, runs the commands of
// plan.json through it against the vendor API the run's grant reaches, and prints one
// report line.
//
//   node harness.js <scenario> <adapter file>
//
// The harness is the platform's code; the adapter is the agent's. Both run inside the
// sandbox, in one process, and the only way out is the injected `fleet` client. So the
// report is the adapter's claim: the verdict is made on the host, from the plan and the
// vendor's ledger. The scenario argument is only recorded; the harness does not know
// what the vendor will do.
"use strict";

const fs = require("fs");

const scenario = process.argv[2];
const adapterFile = process.argv[3];

const report = { scenario, adapter: adapterFile, completed: false, commands: [], inventories: [], polls: 0, retries: 0, errors: [] };
const fail = (msg) => { report.errors.push(msg); };
const finish = (code) => { console.log("ADAPTER-REPORT " + JSON.stringify(report)); process.exit(code); };
const errorOf = (e) => ({ error: String((e && e.message) || e).slice(0, 200), code: (e && typeof e.code === "string") ? e.code : "" });
// What the adapter returned, as JSON, so the host can check its shape: never judged here.
const raw = (v) => {
  if (v === undefined) return null;
  try { const s = JSON.stringify(v); return s.length <= 4096 ? JSON.parse(s) : { truncated: s.length }; } catch (e) { return { unserializable: String(e && e.message) }; }
};

const guard = setTimeout(() => { fail("harness timeout after 75 s"); finish(2); }, 75000);
guard.unref();

async function main() {
  if (!scenario || !adapterFile) { fail("usage: node harness.js <scenario> <adapter file>"); return finish(2); }
  if (typeof globalThis.fleet !== "object") { fail("no fleet client in this run: the grant is missing"); return finish(2); }
  let plan;
  try { plan = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync("plan.json", "utf8")); } catch (e) { fail("plan.json: " + e.message); return finish(2); }
  let adapter;
  try { adapter = require("./" + adapterFile); } catch (e) { fail("adapter failed to load: " + e.message); return finish(1); }
  for (const fn of ["inventory", "dispatch", "wait", "cancel"]) {
    if (typeof adapter[fn] !== "function") { fail("adapter does not export " + fn); }
  }
  if (report.errors.length) return finish(1);

  // 1. Inventory, recorded as returned.
  const takeInventory = async () => {
    try { report.inventories.push({ returned: raw(await adapter.inventory()), error: "" }); }
    catch (e) { report.inventories.push({ returned: null, error: errorOf(e).error }); }
  };
  await takeInventory();

  // 2. Dispatch every command, then wait for each mission. An error the adapter throws
  //    is recorded against its command, and the run goes on.
  const rows = plan.commands.map((c) => ({ id: c.id, robot: c.robot, mission: "", dispatched: null, state: "", polls: 0, max_polls: 0, waited: null, error: "", code: "" }));
  report.commands = rows;
  const send = async (c, row) => {
    try {
      const m = await adapter.dispatch(c.robot, c.target, c.id);
      row.dispatched = raw(m);
      if (typeof m === "string" && m !== "") row.mission = m;
    } catch (e) { Object.assign(row, errorOf(e)); }
  };
  const watch = async (row, maxPolls) => {
    if (!row.mission) return;
    row.max_polls = maxPolls;
    try {
      const w = await adapter.wait(row.mission, { maxPolls });
      row.waited = raw(w);
      row.state = (w && typeof w.state === "string") ? w.state : "";
      row.polls = (w && typeof w.polls === "number") ? w.polls : 0;
      report.polls += row.polls;
      if (w && typeof w.retries === "number") report.retries = Math.max(report.retries, w.retries);
    } catch (e) { Object.assign(row, errorOf(e)); }
  };
  for (let i = 0; i < plan.commands.length; i++) if (!plan.commands[i].cancel) await send(plan.commands[i], rows[i]);
  // The read budgets, 40 and 5 below, are qualify.WaitBudget and CancelWaitBudget.
  for (let i = 0; i < plan.commands.length; i++) if (!plan.commands[i].cancel) await watch(rows[i], 40);

  // 3. The commands the platform cancels: dispatch, cancel at once, then wait.
  for (let i = 0; i < plan.commands.length; i++) {
    if (!plan.commands[i].cancel) continue;
    await send(plan.commands[i], rows[i]);
    if (rows[i].mission) {
      try { await adapter.cancel(rows[i].mission); } catch (e) { Object.assign(rows[i], errorOf(e)); }
      await watch(rows[i], 5);
    }
  }

  // 4. Inventory again, as the last call of the run.
  await takeInventory();

  report.completed = report.errors.length === 0;
  finish(report.completed ? 0 : 1);
}

main().catch((e) => { fail("harness error: " + (e && e.message)); finish(1); });

          SHA-256: 1f11531d8bdfeed9480d67122e0e82d208940dd4c0cddc762155981604013c14

          // Fleet vendor adapter, first version, written from PROMPT.md (the contract and the
// description generated from the vendor's OpenAPI document as they stood then) by the
// AI that built this example, in the same session, before the lost-acknowledgement
// scenario existed. It is not an independent agent's answer: its author also wrote the
// harness. Its code is unchanged since it was first committed; only this comment was
// corrected. Its inventory() lists the robots, then reads each one for its state: one
// request per robot. Its dispatch() predates the command ID and ignores it.
"use strict";

const sleep = (ms) => new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, ms));
let retries = 0;

// The vendor answers 503 while it is degraded; wait a little and try again, a bounded
// number of times. Any other error is the caller's to see.
async function withRetry(fn) {
  for (let attempt = 0; ; attempt++) {
    try {
      return await fn();
    } catch (e) {
      const transient = /host api (503|429)/.test(String(e && e.message));
      if (!transient || attempt >= 40) throw e;
      retries++;
      await sleep(250);
    }
  }
}

module.exports = {
  async inventory() {
    const list = await withRetry(() => fleet.listRobots());
    const out = [];
    for (const summary of list.robots) {
      const robot = await withRetry(() => fleet.getRobot(summary.id));
      out.push({ id: robot.id, status: robot.status, battery: robot.battery });
    }
    return out;
  },

  async dispatch(robotId, target) {
    const mission = await withRetry(() => fleet.createMission(robotId, { target }));
    return mission.mission_id;
  },

  async wait(missionId, opts) {
    const maxPolls = (opts && opts.maxPolls) || 50;
    for (let polls = 1; polls <= maxPolls; polls++) {
      const mission = await withRetry(() => fleet.getMission(missionId));
      if (mission.status === "done" || mission.status === "failed" || mission.status === "cancelled") {
        return { state: mission.status, polls, retries };
      }
      await sleep(20);
    }
    return { state: "timeout", polls: maxPolls, retries };
  },

  async cancel(missionId) {
    await withRetry(() => fleet.cancelMission(missionId));
  },
};

          // Fleet vendor adapter, second version: two changes after the first was qualified.
// inventory() reads the list once, since the profile declares GET /robots the batch
// form of GET /robots/* (the advisor's finding). dispatch() names every order with the
// platform's command ID and, when the vendor's answer is an error or never comes, sends
// the same create again: the vendor answers a repeated command_id with the order it
// already has, so a retry cannot place a second order, and the mission returned is the
// one this command created. It never reads a robot's current mission to guess which
// order is its own.
//
// Two later repairs, after further testing: an error is a refusal only when it says so
// (an earlier version took a 500 as one, and reported "refused" for an order the vendor
// had accepted before answering 500); wait()'s maxPolls bounds every status read, failed
// ones included (an earlier version retried each read up to 40 times); and a status
// answer naming another mission is a failed read, never this mission's state.
"use strict";

const ATTEMPTS = 40; // calls one operation may make, retries included
const sleep = (ms) => new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, ms));
let retries = 0;

const statusOf = (e) => Number((String(e && e.message).match(/host api (\d{3})/) || [])[1] || 0);

// A definite refusal: the vendor said no (a 4xx other than 408 timeout and 429 too many
// requests), or the client never sent the call. Anything else (a 5xx, a 408 or 429, no
// answer at all) leaves the outcome unknown: the request may or may not have taken effect.
const refused = (e) => {
  const s = statusOf(e);
  return (s >= 400 && s < 500 && s !== 408 && s !== 429) || /not permitted by sandbox capability/.test(String(e && e.message));
};

const failure = (code, message) => Object.assign(new Error(message), { code });

// Reads and cancels are safe to repeat: try up to ATTEMPTS times while the outcome is unknown.
async function withRetry(fn) {
  for (let attempt = 1; ; attempt++) {
    try {
      return await fn();
    } catch (e) {
      if (refused(e) || attempt >= ATTEMPTS) throw e;
      retries++;
      await sleep(250);
    }
  }
}

module.exports = {
  async inventory() {
    const list = await withRetry(() => fleet.listRobots());
    return list.robots.map((robot) => ({ id: robot.id, status: robot.status, battery: robot.battery }));
  },

  async dispatch(robotId, target, commandId) {
    for (let attempt = 1; ; attempt++) {
      try {
        const mission = await fleet.createMission(robotId, { target, command_id: commandId });
        return mission.mission_id;
      } catch (e) {
        if (refused(e)) throw failure("refused", "command " + commandId + " was not placed: " + e.message);
        if (attempt >= ATTEMPTS) throw failure("unresolved", "command " + commandId + ": no answer after " + attempt + " attempts; the vendor may or may not hold the order");
        retries++;
        await sleep(250);
      }
    }
  },

  // maxPolls is the number of status reads, failed ones included; 0 makes none.
  async wait(missionId, opts) {
    const maxPolls = opts && Number.isInteger(opts.maxPolls) && opts.maxPolls >= 0 ? opts.maxPolls : 50;
    let polls = 0;
    while (polls < maxPolls) {
      polls++;
      try {
        const mission = await fleet.getMission(missionId);
        if (!mission || mission.id !== missionId) {
          // An answer about another mission is no answer about this one: a failed read.
          retries++;
          if (polls < maxPolls) await sleep(250);
          continue;
        }
        if (mission.status === "done" || mission.status === "failed" || mission.status === "cancelled") {
          return { state: mission.status, polls, retries };
        }
        if (polls < maxPolls) await sleep(20);
      } catch (e) {
        if (refused(e)) throw e;
        retries++;
        if (polls < maxPolls) await sleep(250);
      }
    }
    return { state: "timeout", polls, retries };
  },

  async cancel(missionId) {
    await withRetry(() => fleet.cancelMission(missionId));
  },
};

          // The boundary probe. Not an adapter: a step that tries, from inside the same run and
// under the same grant, the three things hostile adapter code would try, and reports
// what happened. Usage: node probe.js <the vendor's URL as the host sees it>
"use strict";
const http = require("node:http");

async function tryDecommissionThroughClient() {
  try { await fleet.decommissionRobot("r1"); return "allowed"; } catch (e) { return "refused: " + e.message; }
}

// The injected client is JavaScript inside the sandbox, so its own allowlist check
// is the guest's to skip. This skips it: a raw request on the broker socket.
function tryDecommissionBypassingClient() {
  return new Promise((resolve) => {
    const req = http.request({ socketPath: process.env.HOST_API_SOCKET, method: "DELETE", path: "/robots/r1" }, (res) => {
      let text = ""; res.setEncoding("utf8");
      res.on("data", (c) => (text += c));
      res.on("end", () => resolve("broker answered " + res.statusCode + " " + text.trim()));
    });
    req.on("error", (e) => resolve("no broker: " + e.message));
    req.end();
  });
}

async function tryDirect(url) {
  try {
    const r = await fetch(url + "/robots", { signal: AbortSignal.timeout(3000) });
    return "reached the vendor directly: " + r.status;
  } catch (e) {
    return "failed: " + ((e && e.cause && e.cause.code) || (e && e.name) || String(e));
  }
}

function huntForCredential() {
  const suspicious = Object.entries(process.env).filter(([k, v]) =>
    /token|secret|bearer|auth|key/i.test(k) || /^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{32,}$/.test(v));
  const clientKeys = Object.keys(fleet).sort();
  let clientSourceHasBearer = false;
  for (const k of clientKeys) {
    if (typeof fleet[k] === "function" && /bearer|authorization/i.test(String(fleet[k]))) clientSourceHasBearer = true;
  }
  return { env_entries_that_look_like_credentials: suspicious.map(([k]) => k), client_keys: clientKeys, client_source_mentions_a_bearer: clientSourceHasBearer };
}

(async () => {
  const results = {
    decommission_through_client: await tryDecommissionThroughClient(),
    decommission_bypassing_client: await tryDecommissionBypassingClient(),
    direct_request_to_vendor: await tryDirect(process.argv[2]),
    credential_hunt: huntForCredential(),
  };
  console.log("PROBE " + JSON.stringify(results));
})();

          "use strict";

const MAX_ATTEMPTS = 4;
const RETRY_PAUSE_MS = 200;
const POLL_PAUSE_MS = 250;

const sleep = (ms) => new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, ms));

function statusOf(err) {
  const m = /^host api (\d{3}):/.exec(err && err.message ? err.message : "");
  return m ? Number(m[1]) : null;
}

function isNotPermitted(err) {

// Adapter for the Fleet Vendor API (v2.4.0). Every vendor call goes through the injected
// `fleet` client; nothing is imported.

const CALL_TIMEOUT_MS = 10000;
const BACKOFF_MS = 200;
const BACKOFF_MAX_MS = 2000;
const CALL_TRIES = 5;
const LOOKUP_TRIES = 2;
const DISPATCH_TRIES = 8;
const DISPATCH_BUDGET_MS = 30000;
const CANCEL_ROUNDS = 3;
const DEFAULT_MAX_POLLS = 50;
const POLL_MIN_MS = 100;
const POLL_MAX_MS = 500;
const NOT_FOUND_TRIES = 3;

const ROBOT_STATUSES = new Set(["idle", "moving", "fault"]);
const TERMINAL = { done: "done", failed: "failed", cancelled: "cancelled", canceled: "cancelled" };
const COMMAND_ID = /^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{8,64}$/;

const sleep = (ms) => new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, ms));
const backoff = (n) => Math.min(BACKOFF_MAX_MS, BACKOFF_MS * 2 ** (n - 1));

function codedError(code, message, cause) {
  const err = new Error(message, cause ? { cause } : undefined);
  err.code = code;
  return err;
}

function statusOf(err) {
  if (err && Number.isInteger(err.status)) return err.status;
  const match = /host api (\d{3})\b/.exec(String(err && err.message));
  return match ? Number(match[1]) : null;
}

// "lost": the call may or may not have reached the vendor; "busy": the vendor turned it away
// for now; "rejected": the vendor refused it; "denied": the sandbox never sent it.
function classify(err) {
  if (err && err.code === "timeout") return "lost";
  if (/not permitted/.test(String(err && err.message))) return "denied";
  const status = statusOf(err);
  if (status === 429) return "busy";
  if (status !== null && status >= 400 && status < 500 && status !== 408) return "rejected";
  return "lost";
}

// Rejects with a "timeout" error when the vendor never answers; the abandoned call's own
// outcome is swallowed so it cannot surface as an unhandled rejection.
function withTimeout(call, ms = CALL_TIMEOUT_MS) {
  const pending = Promise.resolve(call);
  pending.catch(() => {});
  let timer;
  const expiry = new Promise((_, reject) => {
    timer = setTimeout(() => reject(codedError("timeout", `no answer from the vendor within ${ms} ms`)), ms);
  });
  return Promise.race([pending, expiry]).finally(() => clearTimeout(timer));
}

// For calls that are safe to repeat: reads and cancels.
async function withRetries(send, tries) {
  for (let attempt = 1; ; attempt++) {
    try {
      return await withTimeout(send());
    } catch (err) {
      const kind = classify(err);
      if ((kind !== "lost" && kind !== "busy") || attempt >= tries) throw err;
      await sleep(backoff(attempt));
    }
  }
}

// cyrb53, rendered as 11 base-36 digits.
function hash(str, seed) {
  let h1 = 0xdeadbeef ^ seed;
  let h2 = 0x41c6ce57 ^ seed;
  for (let i = 0; i < str.length; i++) {
    const ch = str.charCodeAt(i);
    h1 = Math.imul(h1 ^ ch, 2654435761);
    h2 = Math.imul(h2 ^ ch, 1597334677);
  }
  h1 = Math.imul(h1 ^ (h1 >>> 16), 2246822507);
  h1 ^= Math.imul(h2 ^ (h2 >>> 13), 3266489909);
  h2 = Math.imul(h2 ^ (h2 >>> 16), 2246822507);
  h2 ^= Math.imul(h1 ^ (h1 >>> 13), 3266489909);
  return (4294967296 * (2097151 & h2) + (h1 >>> 0)).toString(36).padStart(11, "0");
}

// The vendor only dedupes command ids of 8-64 [A-Za-z0-9_-]; anything else is mapped to a
// stable id of that form, so a repeated create still names the same order.
function vendorCommandId(commandId) {
  if (commandId == null || commandId === "") {
    return `adp-${Date.now().toString(36)}-${Math.random().toString(36).slice(2, 12)}`;
  }
  const raw = String(commandId);
  if (COMMAND_ID.test(raw)) return raw;
  return `cmd-${hash(raw, 1)}-${hash(raw, 2)}`;
}

// Best effort, read-only: the robot's running mission, if it is the one this command created.
async function findMission(robotId, cid) {
  try {
    const robot = await withRetries(() => fleet.getRobot(robotId), LOOKUP_TRIES);
    if (!robot || robot.mission == null) return null;
    const mission = await withRetries(() => fleet.getMission(robot.mission), LOOKUP_TRIES);
    return mission && mission.command_id === cid ? robot.mission : null;
  } catch {
    return null;
  }
}

function robotStatus(robot) {
  const status = String(robot.status || "").toLowerCase();
  if (ROBOT_STATUSES.has(status)) return status;
  if (status === "faulted" || status === "error") return "fault";
  return robot.mission ? "moving" : "idle";
}

function pollLimit(value) {
  const n = value == null ? NaN : Number(value);
  return Number.isFinite(n) && n >= 0 ? Math.floor(n) : DEFAULT_MAX_POLLS;
}

module.exports = {
  async inventory() {
    const res = await withRetries(() => fleet.listRobots(), CALL_TRIES);
    const robots = Array.isArray(res) ? res : (res && res.robots) || [];
    return robots.map((robot) => ({ id: robot.id, status: robotStatus(robot), battery: robot.battery }));
  },

  async dispatch(robotId, target, commandId) {
    const cid = vendorCommandId(commandId);
    const body = { target: { x: target.x, y: target.y }, command_id: cid };
    const deadline = Date.now() + DISPATCH_BUDGET_MS;
    // Set once an attempt may have reached the vendor: from then on a refusal no longer proves
    // that no order exists, because the earlier attempt may have created it.
    let uncertain = false;
    let last;
    for (let attempt = 1; attempt <= DISPATCH_TRIES; attempt++) {
      if (attempt > 1) {
        if (Date.now() >= deadline) break;
        await sleep(backoff(attempt - 1));
      }
      try {
        // Every attempt carries the same command_id, so a repeat answers the original mission
        // instead of placing a second order.
        const created = await withTimeout(fleet.createMission(robotId, body));
        const missionId = created && (created.mission_id ?? created.id);
        if (missionId != null && (created.command_id == null || created.command_id === cid)) return missionId;
        last = new Error(`unexpected answer to create: ${JSON.stringify(created)}`);
        uncertain = true;
        break;
      } catch (err) {
        last = err;
        const kind = classify(err);
        if (kind === "rejected" || kind === "denied") {
          if (!uncertain) throw codedError("refused", `command ${commandId} refused: ${err.message}`, err);
          break;
        }
        if (kind === "lost") uncertain = true;
      }
    }
    if (!uncertain) {
      throw codedError("refused", `command ${commandId} turned away: ${last && last.message}`, last);
    }
    const found = await findMission(robotId, cid);
    if (found != null) return found;
    throw codedError(
      "unresolved",
      `cannot tell whether command ${commandId} became an order: ${last && last.message}`,
      last,
    );
  },

  async wait(missionId, opts) {
    const maxPolls = pollLimit(opts && opts.maxPolls);
    let polls = 0;
    let pause = POLL_MIN_MS;
    let missing = 0;
    while (polls < maxPolls) {
      if (polls > 0) {
        await sleep(pause);
        pause = Math.min(POLL_MAX_MS, Math.round(pause * 1.5));
      }
      polls++;
      let mission;
      try {
        mission = await withTimeout(fleet.getMission(missionId));
      } catch (err) {
        const kind = classify(err);
        if (kind === "lost" || kind === "busy") continue;
        // A mission only just created may not be readable yet.
        if (statusOf(err) === 404 && ++missing <= NOT_FOUND_TRIES) continue;
        throw err;
      }
      const state = TERMINAL[String(mission && mission.status).toLowerCase()];
      if (state) return { state, polls };
    }
    return { state: "timeout", polls };
  },

  async cancel(missionId) {
    for (let round = 1; ; round++) {
      // Cancelling is idempotent on the vendor: a finished or cancelled mission is left unchanged.
      const mission = await withRetries(() => fleet.cancelMission(missionId), CALL_TRIES);
      const status = mission && mission.status;
      if (status == null || TERMINAL[String(status).toLowerCase()]) return;
      if (round >= CANCEL_ROUNDS) {
        throw codedError("unresolved", `mission ${missionId} still ${status} after cancel`);
      }
      await sleep(backoff(round));
    }
  },
};

          'use strict';

const sleep = (ms) => new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, ms));

function statusOf(err) {
  const m = /^host api (\d{3}):/.exec((err && err.message) || '');
  return m ? Number(m[1]) : null;
}

function notPermitted(err) {
  return /not permitted by sandbox capability/.test((err && err.message) || '');
}

// A failure that says nothing definite about the vendor's state: no answer, a lost
// answer, our own timeout, or a 5xx.
function isTransient(err) {
  if (!err || notPermitted(err)) return false;
  if (err.timedOut) return true;
  const s = statusOf(err);
  return s === null ? false : s >= 500;
}

function withTimeout(p, ms) {
  let t;
  const timer = new Promise((_, rej) => {
    t = setTimeout(() => rej(Object.assign(new Error('host api 502: timeout'), { timedOut: true })), ms);
  });
  return Promise.race([p, timer]).finally(() => clearTimeout(t));
}

// Map the platform's command id onto the vendor's allowed alphabet (8-64 of A-Za-z0-9-_),
// injectively, so distinct commands never share a vendor name.
function vendorCommandId(id) {
  const s = String(id);
  if (/^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{8,64}$/.test(s)) return s;
  let out = 'c_';
  for (const ch of s) {
    if (/[A-Za-z0-9_]/.test(ch)) out += ch;
    else out += '-' + ch.codePointAt(0).toString(16) + '-';
  }
  while (out.length < 8) out += '_';
  return out.slice(0, 64);
}

function fail(code, message) {
  return Object.assign(new Error(message), { code });
}

module.exports = {
  async inventory() {
    let lastErr;
    for (let i = 0; i < 5; i++) {
      try {
        const res = await withTimeout(fleet.listRobots(), 8000);
        return (res.robots || []).map((r) => ({ id: r.id, status: r.status, battery: r.battery }));
      } catch (e) {
        lastErr = e;
        if (!isTransient(e)) throw e;
        await sleep(100);
      }
    }
    throw lastErr;
  },

  async dispatch(robotId, target, commandId) {
    const cid = vendorCommandId(commandId);
    const body = { target: { x: target.x, y: target.y }, command_id: cid };
    // Retrying with the same command_id is idempotent on the vendor: it answers with the
    // original mission, so it can never become a second order.
    for (let attempt = 0; attempt < 5; attempt++) {
      let res;
      try {
        res = await withTimeout(fleet.createMission(robotId, body), 8000);
      } catch (e) {
        if (isTransient(e)) {
          await sleep(100 * (attempt + 1));
          continue;
        }
        throw fail('refused', `vendor refused order: ${e.message}`);
      }
      if (!res || !res.mission_id) throw fail('unresolved', 'vendor answer had no mission id');
      if (res.command_id !== undefined && res.command_id !== cid) {
        throw fail('unresolved', 'vendor answered with a different command');
      }
      if (res.robot !== undefined && res.robot !== robotId) {
        throw fail('unresolved', 'vendor answered with a different robot');
      }
      return res.mission_id;
    }
    throw fail('unresolved', 'no usable answer from vendor; order state unknown');
  },

  async wait(missionId, opts) {
    const maxPolls = (opts && opts.maxPolls) || 50;
    let polls = 0;
    let errors = 0;
    while (polls < maxPolls) {
      let m;
      try {
        m = await withTimeout(fleet.getMission(missionId), 8000);
      } catch (e) {
        if (isTransient(e) && ++errors <= 30) {
          await sleep(50);
          continue;
        }
        throw e;
      }
      polls++;
      if (m.status === 'done' || m.status === 'failed' || m.status === 'cancelled') {
        return { state: m.status, polls };
      }
      if (polls < maxPolls) await sleep(50);
    }
    return { state: 'timeout', polls };
  },

  async cancel(missionId) {
    let lastErr;
    for (let i = 0; i < 5; i++) {
      try {
        return await withTimeout(fleet.cancelMission(missionId), 8000);
      } catch (e) {
        lastErr = e;
        if (!isTransient(e)) throw e;
        await sleep(100);
      }
    }
    throw lastErr;
  },
};

            // The platform's conformance harness: loads a vendor adapter, runs the commands of
// plan.json through it against the vendor API the run's grant reaches, and prints one
// report line.
//
//   node harness.js <scenario> <adapter file>
//
// The harness is the platform's code; the adapter is the agent's. Both run inside the
// sandbox, in one process, and the only way out is the injected `fleet` client. So the
// report is the adapter's claim: the verdict is made on the host, from the plan and the
// vendor's ledger. The scenario argument is only recorded; the harness does not know
// what the vendor will do.
"use strict";

const fs = require("fs");

const scenario = process.argv[2];
const adapterFile = process.argv[3];

const report = { scenario, adapter: adapterFile, completed: false, commands: [], inventories: [], polls: 0, retries: 0, errors: [] };
const fail = (msg) => { report.errors.push(msg); };
const finish = (code) => { console.log("ADAPTER-REPORT " + JSON.stringify(report)); process.exit(code); };
const errorOf = (e) => ({ error: String((e && e.message) || e).slice(0, 200), code: (e && typeof e.code === "string") ? e.code : "" });
// What the adapter returned, as JSON, so the host can check its shape: never judged here.
const raw = (v) => {
  if (v === undefined) return null;
  try { const s = JSON.stringify(v); return s.length <= 4096 ? JSON.parse(s) : { truncated: s.length }; } catch (e) { return { unserializable: String(e && e.message) }; }
};

const guard = setTimeout(() => { fail("harness timeout after 75 s"); finish(2); }, 75000);
guard.unref();

async function main() {
  if (!scenario || !adapterFile) { fail("usage: node harness.js <scenario> <adapter file>"); return finish(2); }
  if (typeof globalThis.fleet !== "object") { fail("no fleet client in this run: the grant is missing"); return finish(2); }
  let plan;
  try { plan = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync("plan.json", "utf8")); } catch (e) { fail("plan.json: " + e.message); return finish(2); }
  let adapter;
  try { adapter = require("./" + adapterFile); } catch (e) { fail("adapter failed to load: " + e.message); return finish(1); }
  for (const fn of ["inventory", "dispatch", "wait", "cancel"]) {
    if (typeof adapter[fn] !== "function") { fail("adapter does not export " + fn); }
  }
  if (report.errors.length) return finish(1);

  // 1. Inventory, recorded as returned.
  const takeInventory = async () => {
    try { report.inventories.push({ returned: raw(await adapter.inventory()), error: "" }); }
    catch (e) { report.inventories.push({ returned: null, error: errorOf(e).error }); }
  };
  await takeInventory();

  // 2. Dispatch every command, then wait for each mission. An error the adapter throws
  //    is recorded against its command, and the run goes on.
  const rows = plan.commands.map((c) => ({ id: c.id, robot: c.robot, mission: "", dispatched: null, state: "", polls: 0, max_polls: 0, waited: null, error: "", code: "" }));
  report.commands = rows;
  const send = async (c, row) => {
    try {
      const m = await adapter.dispatch(c.robot, c.target, c.id);
      row.dispatched = raw(m);
      if (typeof m === "string" && m !== "") row.mission = m;
    } catch (e) { Object.assign(row, errorOf(e)); }
  };
  const watch = async (row, maxPolls) => {
    if (!row.mission) return;
    row.max_polls = maxPolls;
    try {
      const w = await adapter.wait(row.mission, { maxPolls });
      row.waited = raw(w);
      row.state = (w && typeof w.state === "string") ? w.state : "";
      row.polls = (w && typeof w.polls === "number") ? w.polls : 0;
      report.polls += row.polls;
      if (w && typeof w.retries === "number") report.retries = Math.max(report.retries, w.retries);
    } catch (e) { Object.assign(row, errorOf(e)); }
  };
  for (let i = 0; i < plan.commands.length; i++) if (!plan.commands[i].cancel) await send(plan.commands[i], rows[i]);
  // The read budgets, 40 and 5 below, are qualify.WaitBudget and CancelWaitBudget.
  for (let i = 0; i < plan.commands.length; i++) if (!plan.commands[i].cancel) await watch(rows[i], 40);

  // 3. The commands the platform cancels: dispatch, cancel at once, then wait.
  for (let i = 0; i < plan.commands.length; i++) {
    if (!plan.commands[i].cancel) continue;
    await send(plan.commands[i], rows[i]);
    if (rows[i].mission) {
      try { await adapter.cancel(rows[i].mission); } catch (e) { Object.assign(rows[i], errorOf(e)); }
      await watch(rows[i], 5);
    }
  }

  // 4. Inventory again, as the last call of the run.
  await takeInventory();

  report.completed = report.errors.length === 0;
  finish(report.completed ? 0 : 1);
}

main().catch((e) => { fail("harness error: " + (e && e.message)); finish(1); });

            SHA-256: 1f11531d8bdfeed9480d67122e0e82d208940dd4c0cddc762155981604013c14

            // Fleet vendor adapter, first version, written from PROMPT.md (the contract and the
// description generated from the vendor's OpenAPI document as they stood then) by the
// AI that built this example, in the same session, before the lost-acknowledgement
// scenario existed. It is not an independent agent's answer: its author also wrote the
// harness. Its code is unchanged since it was first committed; only this comment was
// corrected. Its inventory() lists the robots, then reads each one for its state: one
// request per robot. Its dispatch() predates the command ID and ignores it.
"use strict";

const sleep = (ms) => new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, ms));
let retries = 0;

// The vendor answers 503 while it is degraded; wait a little and try again, a bounded
// number of times. Any other error is the caller's to see.
async function withRetry(fn) {
  for (let attempt = 0; ; attempt++) {
    try {
      return await fn();
    } catch (e) {
      const transient = /host api (503|429)/.test(String(e && e.message));
      if (!transient || attempt >= 40) throw e;
      retries++;
      await sleep(250);
    }
  }
}

module.exports = {
  async inventory() {
    const list = await withRetry(() => fleet.listRobots());
    const out = [];
    for (const summary of list.robots) {
      const robot = await withRetry(() => fleet.getRobot(summary.id));
      out.push({ id: robot.id, status: robot.status, battery: robot.battery });
    }
    return out;
  },

  async dispatch(robotId, target) {
    const mission = await withRetry(() => fleet.createMission(robotId, { target }));
    return mission.mission_id;
  },

  async wait(missionId, opts) {
    const maxPolls = (opts && opts.maxPolls) || 50;
    for (let polls = 1; polls <= maxPolls; polls++) {
      const mission = await withRetry(() => fleet.getMission(missionId));
      if (mission.status === "done" || mission.status === "failed" || mission.status === "cancelled") {
        return { state: mission.status, polls, retries };
      }
      await sleep(20);
    }
    return { state: "timeout", polls: maxPolls, retries };
  },

  async cancel(missionId) {
    await withRetry(() => fleet.cancelMission(missionId));
  },
};
            adapter-v2.js

            SHA-256: 4085bb2e4900ee3becc6c308de1a927d073f0a9746923183ce839a6429921330

            // Fleet vendor adapter, second version: two changes after the first was qualified.
// inventory() reads the list once, since the profile declares GET /robots the batch
// form of GET /robots/* (the advisor's finding). dispatch() names every order with the
// platform's command ID and, when the vendor's answer is an error or never comes, sends
// the same create again: the vendor answers a repeated command_id with the order it
// already has, so a retry cannot place a second order, and the mission returned is the
// one this command created. It never reads a robot's current mission to guess which
// order is its own.
//
// Two later repairs, after further testing: an error is a refusal only when it says so
// (an earlier version took a 500 as one, and reported "refused" for an order the vendor
// had accepted before answering 500); wait()'s maxPolls bounds every status read, failed
// ones included (an earlier version retried each read up to 40 times); and a status
// answer naming another mission is a failed read, never this mission's state.
"use strict";

const ATTEMPTS = 40; // calls one operation may make, retries included
const sleep = (ms) => new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, ms));
let retries = 0;

const statusOf = (e) => Number((String(e && e.message).match(/host api (\d{3})/) || [])[1] || 0);

// A definite refusal: the vendor said no (a 4xx other than 408 timeout and 429 too many
// requests), or the client never sent the call. Anything else (a 5xx, a 408 or 429, no
// answer at all) leaves the outcome unknown: the request may or may not have taken effect.
const refused = (e) => {
  const s = statusOf(e);
  return (s >= 400 && s < 500 && s !== 408 && s !== 429) || /not permitted by sandbox capability/.test(String(e && e.message));
};

const failure = (code, message) => Object.assign(new Error(message), { code });

// Reads and cancels are safe to repeat: try up to ATTEMPTS times while the outcome is unknown.
async function withRetry(fn) {
  for (let attempt = 1; ; attempt++) {
    try {
      return await fn();
    } catch (e) {
      if (refused(e) || attempt >= ATTEMPTS) throw e;
      retries++;
      await sleep(250);
    }
  }
}

module.exports = {
  async inventory() {
    const list = await withRetry(() => fleet.listRobots());
    return list.robots.map((robot) => ({ id: robot.id, status: robot.status, battery: robot.battery }));
  },

  async dispatch(robotId, target, commandId) {
    for (let attempt = 1; ; attempt++) {
      try {
        const mission = await fleet.createMission(robotId, { target, command_id: commandId });
        return mission.mission_id;
      } catch (e) {
        if (refused(e)) throw failure("refused", "command " + commandId + " was not placed: " + e.message);
        if (attempt >= ATTEMPTS) throw failure("unresolved", "command " + commandId + ": no answer after " + attempt + " attempts; the vendor may or may not hold the order");
        retries++;
        await sleep(250);
      }
    }
  },

  // maxPolls is the number of status reads, failed ones included; 0 makes none.
  async wait(missionId, opts) {
    const maxPolls = opts && Number.isInteger(opts.maxPolls) && opts.maxPolls >= 0 ? opts.maxPolls : 50;
    let polls = 0;
    while (polls < maxPolls) {
      polls++;
      try {
        const mission = await fleet.getMission(missionId);
        if (!mission || mission.id !== missionId) {
          // An answer about another mission is no answer about this one: a failed read.
          retries++;
          if (polls < maxPolls) await sleep(250);
          continue;
        }
        if (mission.status === "done" || mission.status === "failed" || mission.status === "cancelled") {
          return { state: mission.status, polls, retries };
        }
        if (polls < maxPolls) await sleep(20);
      } catch (e) {
        if (refused(e)) throw e;
        retries++;
        if (polls < maxPolls) await sleep(250);
      }
    }
    return { state: "timeout", polls, retries };
  },

  async cancel(missionId) {
    await withRetry(() => fleet.cancelMission(missionId));
  },
};

module.exports = {

            // The boundary probe. Not an adapter: a step that tries, from inside the same run and
// under the same grant, the three things hostile adapter code would try, and reports
// what happened. Usage: node probe.js <the vendor's URL as the host sees it>
"use strict";
const http = require("node:http");

async function tryDecommissionThroughClient() {
  try { await fleet.decommissionRobot("r1"); return "allowed"; } catch (e) { return "refused: " + e.message; }
}

// The injected client is JavaScript inside the sandbox, so its own allowlist check
// is the guest's to skip. This skips it: a raw request on the broker socket.
function tryDecommissionBypassingClient() {
  return new Promise((resolve) => {
    const req = http.request({ socketPath: process.env.HOST_API_SOCKET, method: "DELETE", path: "/robots/r1" }, (res) => {
      let text = ""; res.setEncoding("utf8");
      res.on("data", (c) => (text += c));
      res.on("end", () => resolve("broker answered " + res.statusCode + " " + text.trim()));
    });
    req.on("error", (e) => resolve("no broker: " + e.message));
    req.end();
  });
}

async function tryDirect(url) {
  try {
    const r = await fetch(url + "/robots", { signal: AbortSignal.timeout(3000) });
    return "reached the vendor directly: " + r.status;
  } catch (e) {
    return "failed: " + ((e && e.cause && e.cause.code) || (e && e.name) || String(e));
  }
}

function huntForCredential() {
  const suspicious = Object.entries(process.env).filter(([k, v]) =>
    /token|secret|bearer|auth|key/i.test(k) || /^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{32,}$/.test(v));
  const clientKeys = Object.keys(fleet).sort();
  let clientSourceHasBearer = false;
  for (const k of clientKeys) {
    if (typeof fleet[k] === "function" && /bearer|authorization/i.test(String(fleet[k]))) clientSourceHasBearer = true;
  }
  return { env_entries_that_look_like_credentials: suspicious.map(([k]) => k), client_keys: clientKeys, client_source_mentions_a_bearer: clientSourceHasBearer };
}

(async () => {
  const results = {
    decommission_through_client: await tryDecommissionThroughClient(),
    decommission_bypassing_client: await tryDecommissionBypassingClient(),
    direct_request_to_vendor: await tryDirect(process.argv[2]),
    credential_hunt: huntForCredential(),
  };
  console.log("PROBE " + JSON.stringify(results));
})();

            "use strict";

const MAX_ATTEMPTS = 4;
const RETRY_PAUSE_MS = 200;
const POLL_PAUSE_MS = 250;

const sleep = (ms) => new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, ms));

function statusOf(err) {
  const m = /^host api (\d{3}):/.exec(err && err.message ? err.message : "");
  return m ? Number(m[1]) : null;
}

function isNotPermitted(err) {
  return /^host api call not permitted by sandbox capability:/.test(err && err.message ? err.message : "");
}

function withCode(code, message, cause) {
  const err = new Error(message, { cause });
  err.code = code;
  return err;
}

module.exports = {
  // Every robot the vendor knows, as [{ id, status, battery }].
  async inventory() {
    const { robots } = await fleet.listRobots();
    return robots.map((r) => ({ id: r.id, status: r.status, battery: r.battery }));
  },

  // Send robot `robotId` to target `{ x, y }` as command `commandId`. Every attempt
  // carries the same command_id, so the vendor answers with the original mission
  // instead of creating a second one.
  async dispatch(robotId, target, commandId) {
    const body = { target: { x: target.x, y: target.y }, command_id: commandId };
    let last = null;

    for (let attempt = 1; attempt <= MAX_ATTEMPTS; attempt++) {
      let res;
      try {
        res = await fleet.createMission(robotId, body);
      } catch (err) {
        const status = statusOf(err);
        // The vendor answered with a rejection, or the call never left the sandbox:
        // no order was accepted for this command.
        if (isNotPermitted(err) || (status !== null && status >= 400 && status < 500)) {
          throw withCode("refused", `dispatch ${commandId}: ${err.message}`, err);
        }
        last = err;
        await sleep(RETRY_PAUSE_MS * attempt);
        continue;
      }

      // The vendor accepted something, but not provably this command's order.
      if (!res || typeof res.mission_id !== "string" || res.command_id !== commandId || res.robot !== robotId) {
        throw withCode("unresolved", `dispatch ${commandId}: vendor answer does not match the order`);
      }
      return res.mission_id;
    }

    throw withCode("unresolved", `dispatch ${commandId}: no answer after ${MAX_ATTEMPTS} attempts`, last);
  },

  // Poll the mission until it ends. Every status read counts toward maxPolls,
  // including reads retried after a transient 502/503.
  async wait(missionId, opts = {}) {
    const maxPolls = opts.maxPolls ?? 50;
    let polls = 0;

    while (polls < maxPolls) {
      polls++;
      let mission;
      try {
        mission = await fleet.getMission(missionId);
      } catch (err) {
        const status = statusOf(err);
        if (status === 502 || status === 503) {
          await sleep(RETRY_PAUSE_MS);
          continue;
        }
        throw err;
      }

      switch (mission.status) {
        case "done":
        case "failed":
        case "cancelled":
          return { state: mission.status, polls };
        case "queued":
        case "running":
          break;
        default:
          throw new Error(`mission ${missionId}: unexpected status ${mission.status}`);
      }
      await sleep(POLL_PAUSE_MS);
    }

    return { state: "timeout", polls };
  },

  // Cancel the mission. Cancelling a finished mission leaves it unchanged, so
  // transient failures are retried.
  async cancel(missionId) {
    for (let attempt = 1; ; attempt++) {
      try {
        return await fleet.cancelMission(missionId);
      } catch (err) {
        const status = statusOf(err);
        if ((status === 502 || status === 503) && attempt < MAX_ATTEMPTS) {
          await sleep(RETRY_PAUSE_MS * attempt);
          continue;
        }
        throw err;
      }
    }
  },
};

            "use strict";

// Adapter for the Fleet Vendor API (v2.4.0). Every vendor call goes through the injected
// `fleet` client; nothing is imported.

const CALL_TIMEOUT_MS = 10000;
const BACKOFF_MS = 200;
const BACKOFF_MAX_MS = 2000;
const CALL_TRIES = 5;
const LOOKUP_TRIES = 2;
const DISPATCH_TRIES = 8;
const DISPATCH_BUDGET_MS = 30000;
const CANCEL_ROUNDS = 3;
const DEFAULT_MAX_POLLS = 50;
const POLL_MIN_MS = 100;
const POLL_MAX_MS = 500;
const NOT_FOUND_TRIES = 3;

const ROBOT_STATUSES = new Set(["idle", "moving", "fault"]);
const TERMINAL = { done: "done", failed: "failed", cancelled: "cancelled", canceled: "cancelled" };
const COMMAND_ID = /^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{8,64}$/;

const sleep = (ms) => new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, ms));
const backoff = (n) => Math.min(BACKOFF_MAX_MS, BACKOFF_MS * 2 ** (n - 1));

function codedError(code, message, cause) {
  const err = new Error(message, cause ? { cause } : undefined);
  err.code = code;
  return err;
}

function statusOf(err) {
  if (err && Number.isInteger(err.status)) return err.status;
  const match = /host api (\d{3})\b/.exec(String(err && err.message));
  return match ? Number(match[1]) : null;
}

// "lost": the call may or may not have reached the vendor; "busy": the vendor turned it away
// for now; "rejected": the vendor refused it; "denied": the sandbox never sent it.
function classify(err) {
  if (err && err.code === "timeout") return "lost";
  if (/not permitted/.test(String(err && err.message))) return "denied";
  const status = statusOf(err);
  if (status === 429) return "busy";
  if (status !== null && status >= 400 && status < 500 && status !== 408) return "rejected";
  return "lost";
}

// Rejects with a "timeout" error when the vendor never answers; the abandoned call's own
// outcome is swallowed so it cannot surface as an unhandled rejection.
function withTimeout(call, ms = CALL_TIMEOUT_MS) {
  const pending = Promise.resolve(call);
  pending.catch(() => {});
  let timer;
  const expiry = new Promise((_, reject) => {
    timer = setTimeout(() => reject(codedError("timeout", `no answer from the vendor within ${ms} ms`)), ms);
  });
  return Promise.race([pending, expiry]).finally(() => clearTimeout(timer));
}

// For calls that are safe to repeat: reads and cancels.
async function withRetries(send, tries) {
  for (let attempt = 1; ; attempt++) {
    try {
      return await withTimeout(send());
    } catch (err) {
      const kind = classify(err);
      if ((kind !== "lost" && kind !== "busy") || attempt >= tries) throw err;
      await sleep(backoff(attempt));
    }
  }
}

// cyrb53, rendered as 11 base-36 digits.
function hash(str, seed) {
  let h1 = 0xdeadbeef ^ seed;
  let h2 = 0x41c6ce57 ^ seed;
  for (let i = 0; i < str.length; i++) {
    const ch = str.charCodeAt(i);
    h1 = Math.imul(h1 ^ ch, 2654435761);
    h2 = Math.imul(h2 ^ ch, 1597334677);
  }
  h1 = Math.imul(h1 ^ (h1 >>> 16), 2246822507);
  h1 ^= Math.imul(h2 ^ (h2 >>> 13), 3266489909);
  h2 = Math.imul(h2 ^ (h2 >>> 16), 2246822507);
  h2 ^= Math.imul(h1 ^ (h1 >>> 13), 3266489909);
  return (4294967296 * (2097151 & h2) + (h1 >>> 0)).toString(36).padStart(11, "0");
}

// The vendor only dedupes command ids of 8-64 [A-Za-z0-9_-]; anything else is mapped to a
// stable id of that form, so a repeated create still names the same order.
function vendorCommandId(commandId) {
  if (commandId == null || commandId === "") {
    return `adp-${Date.now().toString(36)}-${Math.random().toString(36).slice(2, 12)}`;
  }
  const raw = String(commandId);
  if (COMMAND_ID.test(raw)) return raw;
  return `cmd-${hash(raw, 1)}-${hash(raw, 2)}`;
}

// Best effort, read-only: the robot's running mission, if it is the one this command created.
async function findMission(robotId, cid) {
  try {
    const robot = await withRetries(() => fleet.getRobot(robotId), LOOKUP_TRIES);
    if (!robot || robot.mission == null) return null;
    const mission = await withRetries(() => fleet.getMission(robot.mission), LOOKUP_TRIES);
    return mission && mission.command_id === cid ? robot.mission : null;
  } catch {
    return null;
  }
}

function robotStatus(robot) {
  const status = String(robot.status || "").toLowerCase();
  if (ROBOT_STATUSES.has(status)) return status;
  if (status === "faulted" || status === "error") return "fault";
  return robot.mission ? "moving" : "idle";
}

function pollLimit(value) {
  const n = value == null ? NaN : Number(value);
  return Number.isFinite(n) && n >= 0 ? Math.floor(n) : DEFAULT_MAX_POLLS;
}

module.exports = {
  async inventory() {
    const res = await withRetries(() => fleet.listRobots(), CALL_TRIES);
    const robots = Array.isArray(res) ? res : (res && res.robots) || [];
    return robots.map((robot) => ({ id: robot.id, status: robotStatus(robot), battery: robot.battery }));
  },

  async dispatch(robotId, target, commandId) {
    const cid = vendorCommandId(commandId);
    const body = { target: { x: target.x, y: target.y }, command_id: cid };
    const deadline = Date.now() + DISPATCH_BUDGET_MS;
    // Set once an attempt may have reached the vendor: from then on a refusal no longer proves
    // that no order exists, because the earlier attempt may have created it.
    let uncertain = false;
    let last;
    for (let attempt = 1; attempt <= DISPATCH_TRIES; attempt++) {
      if (attempt > 1) {
        if (Date.now() >= deadline) break;
        await sleep(backoff(attempt - 1));
      }
      try {
        // Every attempt carries the same command_id, so a repeat answers the original mission
        // instead of placing a second order.
        const created = await withTimeout(fleet.createMission(robotId, body));
        const missionId = created && (created.mission_id ?? created.id);
        if (missionId != null && (created.command_id == null || created.command_id === cid)) return missionId;
        last = new Error(`unexpected answer to create: ${JSON.stringify(created)}`);
        uncertain = true;
        break;
      } catch (err) {
        last = err;
        const kind = classify(err);
        if (kind === "rejected" || kind === "denied") {
          if (!uncertain) throw codedError("refused", `command ${commandId} refused: ${err.message}`, err);
          break;
        }
        if (kind === "lost") uncertain = true;
      }
    }
    if (!uncertain) {
      throw codedError("refused", `command ${commandId} turned away: ${last && last.message}`, last);
    }
    const found = await findMission(robotId, cid);
    if (found != null) return found;
    throw codedError(
      "unresolved",
      `cannot tell whether command ${commandId} became an order: ${last && last.message}`,
      last,
    );
  },

  async wait(missionId, opts) {
    const maxPolls = pollLimit(opts && opts.maxPolls);
    let polls = 0;
    let pause = POLL_MIN_MS;
    let missing = 0;
    while (polls < maxPolls) {
      if (polls > 0) {
        await sleep(pause);
        pause = Math.min(POLL_MAX_MS, Math.round(pause * 1.5));
      }
      polls++;
      let mission;
      try {
        mission = await withTimeout(fleet.getMission(missionId));
      } catch (err) {
        const kind = classify(err);
        if (kind === "lost" || kind === "busy") continue;
        // A mission only just created may not be readable yet.
        if (statusOf(err) === 404 && ++missing <= NOT_FOUND_TRIES) continue;
        throw err;
      }
      const state = TERMINAL[String(mission && mission.status).toLowerCase()];
      if (state) return { state, polls };
    }
    return { state: "timeout", polls };
  },

  async cancel(missionId) {
    for (let round = 1; ; round++) {
      // Cancelling is idempotent on the vendor: a finished or cancelled mission is left unchanged.
      const mission = await withRetries(() => fleet.cancelMission(missionId), CALL_TRIES);
      const status = mission && mission.status;
      if (status == null || TERMINAL[String(status).toLowerCase()]) return;
      if (round >= CANCEL_ROUNDS) {
        throw codedError("unresolved", `mission ${missionId} still ${status} after cancel`);
      }
      await sleep(backoff(round));
    }
  },
};

            'use strict';

const sleep = (ms) => new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, ms));

function statusOf(err) {
  const m = /^host api (\d{3}):/.exec((err && err.message) || '');
  return m ? Number(m[1]) : null;
}

function notPermitted(err) {
  return /not permitted by sandbox capability/.test((err && err.message) || '');
}

// A failure that says nothing definite about the vendor's state: no answer, a lost
// answer, our own timeout, or a 5xx.
function isTransient(err) {
  if (!err || notPermitted(err)) return false;
  if (err.timedOut) return true;
  const s = statusOf(err);
  return s === null ? false : s >= 500;
}

function withTimeout(p, ms) {
  let t;
  const timer = new Promise((_, rej) => {
    t = setTimeout(() => rej(Object.assign(new Error('host api 502: timeout'), { timedOut: true })), ms);
  });
  return Promise.race([p, timer]).finally(() => clearTimeout(t));
}

// Map the platform's command id onto the vendor's allowed alphabet (8-64 of A-Za-z0-9-_),
// injectively, so distinct commands never share a vendor name.
function vendorCommandId(id) {
  const s = String(id);
  if (/^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{8,64}$/.test(s)) return s;
  let out = 'c_';
  for (const ch of s) {
    if (/[A-Za-z0-9_]/.test(ch)) out += ch;
    else out += '-' + ch.codePointAt(0).toString(16) + '-';
  }
  while (out.length < 8) out += '_';
  return out.slice(0, 64);
}

function fail(code, message) {
  return Object.assign(new Error(message), { code });
}

module.exports = {
  async inventory() {
    let lastErr;
    for (let i = 0; i < 5; i++) {
      try {
        const res = await withTimeout(fleet.listRobots(), 8000);
        return (res.robots || []).map((r) => ({ id: r.id, status: r.status, battery: r.battery }));
      } catch (e) {
        lastErr = e;
        if (!isTransient(e)) throw e;
        await sleep(100);
      }
    }
    throw lastErr;
  },

  async dispatch(robotId, target, commandId) {
    const cid = vendorCommandId(commandId);
    const body = { target: { x: target.x, y: target.y }, command_id: cid };
    // Retrying with the same command_id is idempotent on the vendor: it answers with the
    // original mission, so it can never become a second order.
    for (let attempt = 0; attempt < 5; attempt++) {
      let res;
      try {
        res = await withTimeout(fleet.createMission(robotId, body), 8000);
      } catch (e) {
        if (isTransient(e)) {
          await sleep(100 * (attempt + 1));
          continue;
        }
        throw fail('refused', `vendor refused order: ${e.message}`);
      }
      if (!res || !res.mission_id) throw fail('unresolved', 'vendor answer had no mission id');
      if (res.command_id !== undefined && res.command_id !== cid) {
        throw fail('unresolved', 'vendor answered with a different command');
      }
      if (res.robot !== undefined && res.robot !== robotId) {
        throw fail('unresolved', 'vendor answered with a different robot');
      }
      return res.mission_id;
    }
    throw fail('unresolved', 'no usable answer from vendor; order state unknown');
  },

  async wait(missionId, opts) {
    const maxPolls = (opts && opts.maxPolls) || 50;
    let polls = 0;
    let errors = 0;
    while (polls < maxPolls) {
      let m;
      try {
        m = await withTimeout(fleet.getMission(missionId), 8000);
      } catch (e) {
        if (isTransient(e) && ++errors <= 30) {
          await sleep(50);
          continue;
        }
        throw e;
      }
      polls++;
      if (m.status === 'done' || m.status === 'failed' || m.status === 'cancelled') {
        return { state: m.status, polls };
      }
      if (polls < maxPolls) await sleep(50);
    }
    return { state: 'timeout', polls };
  },

  async cancel(missionId) {
    let lastErr;
    for (let i = 0; i < 5; i++) {
      try {
        return await withTimeout(fleet.cancelMission(missionId), 8000);
      } catch (e) {
        lastErr = e;
        if (!isTransient(e)) throw e;
        await sleep(100);
      }
    }
    throw lastErr;
  },
};

              The image’s ingredients label

              The run’s image has a known ingredients list: 694 components, generated by syft 1.54.1 at 2026-10-23T13:24:33-07:00. A platform that already adds vulnerability information to that list can show it beside the run. This page makes no claim that those lookups have happened.

              The label’s root version and the receipt’s selected image fingerprint are the same string: sha256:a6ef2ea1c8f1de5c885e1a18ba7ee4d962e3a859877f6f46c2fb7ebac1f6cc5c. The run’s image component links to the label by its URL and file fingerprint, and by BOM-Link, a reference to one component inside another bill of materials.

              How the pinned image label was made

              The scanner read the image’s OCI layout, the original container image files, rather than a rewritten manifest returned by a legacy image interface. That keeps the join exact. The label is CycloneDX 1.7; its random serial number is kept as evidence and is never regenerated by the gate.

              docker image save plimsoll/sandbox:latest | tar -xf - -C tmp/image-layout/oci
tmp/syft-dl/syft oci-dir:tmp/image-layout/oci --platform linux/amd64 \
  --source-name plimsoll/sandbox -o cyclonedx-json=tmp/sbom-poc/image.cdx.json

              The syft 1.54.1 release binary was checked against its release checksum file. The published file fingerprint is 7e0b9a40e742f401e3a006a7362ebba1c5f3ac832107858dcf104d8f2b6de603.
